transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-30
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Rossi (Redwood SE), Sara Lin (Novus Head of ML), Rajiv Kapoor (Novus Infra), Emily Ortiz (Novus CTO), Ben Morales (Novus SRE)

Summary: Novus is currently on OpenAI for gen and embeddings, exploring Dedicated to reduce unit cost and get predictable latency for synchronous product flows. They run a mix of chat and retrieval-augmented-generation, heavy short-turn latency requirements, and have internal infra using vLLM and TGI for local model hosting for some workloads. Main asks: compatibility with prompts/evals, migration costs, private networking (VPC), KMS and audit logs, and performance parity across their eval sets.

Topics: compatibility, eval parity, dedicated sizing, security (VPC/KMS/SOC2), timeline, benchmarks

Action items (recap at end): Maya to send pricing, Omar to share benchmark plan, Customer to share prompt sets

Transcript body:
[00:00:03] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood inference, i'll kick us off - quick intros?
[00:00:12] Sara Lin: sara here, head of ml at novus, we own prompts, evals, and model selection.
[00:00:18] Rajiv Kapoor: rajiv infra, i handle cloud and networking.
[00:00:21] Emily Ortiz: emily, cto, oversight on infra decisions.
[00:00:25] Ben Morales: ben, sre, i'll be running any benchmarks with our infra.
[00:00:30] Omar Patel: omar, solutions eng at redwood - i'll go deep on perf and compat questions.
[00:00:36] Lena Rossi: lena, i'll follow up on security docs and onboarding.

[00:00:40] Maya Chen: cool, goal for today is to understand your current stack and see how we can map to dedicated or private deployments and run an eval - especially around latency/cost tradeoffs.

[00:00:50] Sara Lin: high level - we use openai for most of our prod calls, embeddings for search, and a small set of on-prem models via vLLM for pre-processing. We're seeing token costs creep up and some flakiness during peaks; also want lower p99 latency.

[00:01:08] Omar Patel: got it. when you say vLLM on-prem, is that for inference-only workloads or training?
[00:01:13] Sara Lin: inference only, mainly short-turn chat generation with avg length ~60 tokens. We also run rags with 3-4 embedding calls per user request.

[00:01:25] Rajiv Kapoor: for infra: we run in GCP, but have a few services in Azure. We're open to redwood dedicated in a region close to our GCP projects or private vpc.

[00:01:35] Emily Ortiz: timeline: want to decide by mid-july, ideally pilot in july and production by q3 if numbers look good.

[00:01:44] Maya Chen: that timeline is realistic. quick compatibility question: are you tied to OpenAI API shapes? any function-calling or specific tooling?

[00:01:52] Sara Lin: we use function calling a bit, and rely on ChatCompletions-ish flows; plus custom sampling settings. Our eval harness assumes identical inputs across providers to check parity.

[00:02:05] Omar Patel: Redwood's Hosted API is compatible with common REST shapes, and Dedicated can expose the same API on-prem - we also support streaming and function-calling. There are sometimes tokenizer or sampling differences across model runtimes (vLLM vs our optimized runtime), so eval parity is something we watch for.

[00:02:22] Sara Lin: that's a concern - we need to ensure our eval pass rates are similar, otherwise behavioral drift for users.

[00:02:27] Omar Patel: understood. typical approach: we run your eval prompt set against our candidate model on dedicated, compare metrics (BLEU-ish, embed distance, human labels). we can also run baseline OpenAI runs side-by-side.

[00:02:40] Ben Morales: what's the typical delta in latency moving from OpenAI to dedicated? Our SLO is p95 < 300ms for the chat path.

[00:02:48] Omar Patel: depends on model variant, batching, and infrastructure. For short-turn workloads, dedicated with GPU-backed nodes and minimal batching can hit median ~80-120ms and p95 ~200-300ms depending on seq length and KV cache hit. There is some tuning with batching to balance throughput.

[00:03:08] Sara Lin: ok that sounds promising. cost wise - we pay X per token now, what's the break-even for dedicated?

[00:03:16] Maya Chen: rough math: for steady high volume it's usually cheaper to commit capacity; for your traffic profile we estimate savings of 30-50% net when you include embedding workloads - we'll send a detailed sizing/pricing sheet.

[00:03:29] Rajiv Kapoor: data residency and encryption - we need KMS, customer-managed keys, audit logs, and SSO (SAML). Also must prove SOC2 and support for private networking or VPC peering.

[00:03:40] Lena Rossi: confirmed - Redwood Private and Dedicated support customer KMS, audit logs, and SAML; we have SOC 2 Type II. we'll share the security pack.

[00:03:50] Emily Ortiz: what's the network setup look like for Dedicated? can we do VPC peering and restrict egress?

[00:03:56] Omar Patel: yes, dedicated can be deployed into an isolated VPC with peering and strict egress rules; for Private on-prem we can also run the control plane in a customer-managed VPC, depending on the package.

[00:04:10] Speaker 1: (unintelligible) - there was a brief question about the control plane and logs.

[00:04:15] Maya Chen: logs: we provide audit logs and operational metrics, and for private setups you can ship logs to your SIEM; we can surface token-level traces in console for debugging.

[00:04:24] Sara Lin: good. about compatibility again - we run a few workloads on TGI in-house, and our wrapper relies on some TGI-specific flags. How portable are prompts/params?

[00:04:34] Omar Patel: TGI and vLLM have small runtime differences; we maintain compatible parameter mappings and our SDK includes helpers to translate. In a few cases, sampling seeds and tokenizer implementations cause micro-differences. For strict parity we usually: 1) match tokenizer + model weights where possible, 2) run evals and adjust sampling/temperature to align output distributions.

[00:04:54] Sara Lin: ok so it's not a drop-in 100% but you have a process. we'll want to see the eval results.

[00:04:59] Ben Morales: for the benchmark run - what do you need from our side?

[00:05:03] Omar Patel: best is a representative prompt set, a replay of traffic profile (qps and concurrency), and sample input sizes; we'll provide a runbook with scripts. we can instrument the runs with p95/p99 and token cost breakdowns.

[00:05:16] Rajiv Kapoor: and what about model hosting - can we bring our own weights to Dedicated?

[00:05:20] Maya Chen: yes, customers can bring their own models; we support common formats (HF-style weights). For private/on-prem there's more control; for hosted/dedicated we have onboarding for custom weights and vetting for compatibility.

[00:05:31] Sara Lin: licensing and compliance: some of our models have specific license terms - will redwood handle that?

[00:05:36] Lena Rossi: we have a model onboarding checklist and legal review for custom weights; we'll include that in the security pack.

[00:05:42] Speaker 2: small question on rollout strategy - can you do canary traffic and automatic fallback to hosted?

[00:05:47] Omar Patel: yep, Redwood supports canary rollouts, A/B tests, and fallback policies. you can route by region, model variant, or cost tier. our routing layer can auto-failover to a compatible hosted model if dedicated capacity is exhausted.

[00:06:00] Emily Ortiz: what about observability - we need per-route latency, cost, and tracing for debugging.

[00:06:05] Maya Chen: Redwood Console shows per-route metrics, token/latency breakdowns, tracing hooks, and error analytics. we can also export metrics to prometheus/grafana.

[00:06:15] Sara Lin: acceptable. i'm worried about eval parity for a few edge-case prompts that are safety-sensitive - any support for human review tools?

[00:06:22] Omar Patel: we offer eval tooling and can integrate human-in-the-loop labeling for a sample set to check for regressions. plus regression alerts tied to eval thresholds.

[00:06:33] Ben Morales: ok logistic q: what does onboarding look like and how long?

[00:06:37] Maya Chen: pilot onboarding - typically 1-2 weeks to provision dedicated capacity and run initial benchmarks, then iterative tuning. private/on-prem longer, depending on network/firewall approvals.

[00:06:48] Sara Lin: good to know. is there a minimum commit for dedicated?

[00:06:52] Maya Chen: yes there's a reserved capacity contract for Dedicated; we can share options from monthly to annual commitments. pilot can be on trial capacity or a short-term reserved pack.

[00:06:59] Rajiv Kapoor: can you support our requirement to rotate KMS keys monthly and maintain immutable audit trails for specific datasets?

[00:07:05] Lena Rossi: we support customer-managed KMS rotation and immutable audit logs; we'll include sample retention policies in the pack.

[00:07:12] Speaker 3: (crosstalk) okay thanks -

[00:07:15] Maya Chen: next steps proposal: we'll send a pricing + sizing sheet, security pack, and benchmark runbook; then schedule a 2-hour benchmark next week where we run your prompt set against Dedicated and OpenAI baseline.

[00:07:27] Sara Lin: sounds good. i can share the prompt set and traffic profile by end of day thursday.

[00:07:34] Ben Morales: we'll provision a test environment and coordinate on the run.

[00:07:38] Emily Ortiz: if the pilot looks good, we'll engage procurement for a reserved capacity commitment.

[00:07:43] Maya Chen: perfect. any final questions?

[00:07:46] Sara Lin: none from me. looking forward to the benchmark.

[00:07:49] Rajiv Kapoor: no more from infra.

[00:07:51] Omar Patel: i'll follow up with the runbook and a slack invite for the test channel.

[00:07:56] Lena Rossi: i'll attach SOC 2 and the network diagram.

[00:08:00] Meeting close

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard words and short crosstalk, some speaker labels generic - cleaned lightly but left verbatim speech patterns.

End of transcript.
